chapters.main_concept: Halogenoalkanes are made from alkanes, alkenes or alcohols and react mainly by nucleophilic substitution (SN1 vs SN2 depending on structure) or beta-elimination (E1/E2). Reactivity follows C-X bond strength (R-I > R-Br > R-Cl > R-F); halogenoarenes are far less reactive because of C-X delocalisation.

chapters.main_concept: The polar C=O group makes aldehydes and ketones susceptible to nucleophilic addition; aldehydes are also easily oxidised, giving the classic Tollens'/Fehling's tests. Carboxylic acids are made by oxidation or hydrolysis, show acidity tuned by inductive effects, and form esters and acyl chlorides whose hydrolysis rates are compared with alkyl and aryl chlorides.
